properties.areaDesc: Coastal Bryan; Coastal Chatham; Coastal Liberty; Coastal McIntosh; Beaufort; Coastal Colleton; Charleston; Coastal Jasper
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 24 at 8:47AM EDT until October 24 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Charleston SC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 1 to 5
feet expected in the surf zone.

* WHERE...South Carolina Beaches, and Georgia Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, until 8 PM EDT this
evening. For the High Surf Advisory, from 2 PM this afternoon
to 5 PM EDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Rio Grande, CO
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 24 at 6:47AM MDT until October 24 at 10:00PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in
Colorado...

Rio Grande Near Del Norte affecting Rio Grande County.

.High flows and flooding will continue along the Rio Grande through
Del Norte.  The river levels will continue to fall but remain in
minor flood stage this morning.

For the Upper Rio Grande River...including Del Norte,.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring.

* WHERE...Rio Grande  near Del Norte.

* WHEN...Until this evening.

* IMPACTS...At 5.5 feet, Minor Flood. The Del Norte Riverwalk Trail
floods.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 6:17 AM MDT Saturday the stage was 5.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 5.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 6:17 AM MDT Saturday was 6.4 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage late
this morning and continue falling to 3.2 feet Wednesday evening.
- Flood stage is 5.5 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 5.6
feet on 06/10/1980.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 700 PM MDT.

properties.areaDesc: San Francisco; North Bay Interior Valleys; San Francisco Bay Shoreline; Northern Monterey Bay; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 24 at 5:46AM PDT until October 29 at 3:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 1.9ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Bay Shoreline locations of San Francisco Bay, Monterey
Bay and Big Sur Coast.

* WHEN...From 8 AM Saturday to 3 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.1 ft above normal (6.9 ft MLLW) at 10:39 AM
Saturday 10/24, 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 11:07 AM
Sunday 10/25, 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 11:39 AM
Monday 10/26, 1.8 ft above normal (7.6 ft MLLW) at 12:15 PM
Tuesday 10/27, 1.9 ft above normal (7.7 ft MLLW) at 12:56 PM
Wednesday 10/28, and 1.7 ft above normal (7.5 ft MLLW) at 01:43
PM Thursday 10/29. These predictions include up to 1.0 ft of
surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding
threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along
the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay,
respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

NWSheadline: COASTAL FLOOD ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 3 PM PDT THURSDAY

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 24 at 6:01AM MDT until October 25 at 6:00AM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of south central New Mexico and the Tularosa
Basin, including Otero County. Far west Texas including El Paso and
Hudspeth Counties.

* WHEN...Saturday evening through early Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Several rounds of thunderstorms are expected to move through
South-Central New Mexico and Far West Texas. Widespread rainfall
amounts of 1" are likely with localized areas receiving 2-3"
resulting in flash flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.
